Codex uses the login of the CLI itself (codex login) and Antigravity uses the local server of the open IDE — neither one asks for a key here.
Data that is not a secret, but the API requires — such as the xAI team. It can come from here, from config.json or from the credentials file itself (XAI_TEAM_ID).
For services that authenticate by login instead of a key. The token is looked up in the JSON, at any level; nothing is copied to the cache.
OAuth token in a JSON file
OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY — the Go plan key (Zen does not work)
The key goes to the system keyring (gnome-keyring) and is read by the collector at query time. The field is cleared after saving.
Use it when the keys are already in a file of yours, at any path (for example ~/.env or ~/.config/secrets.env). The file is read without a shell.
XAI_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY — the Console management key → Settings → Management Keys (the inference one does not work)
